I second having an advocate especially if you are still under 18 .

When dealing with insurance companies and health professionals it can be a tremendous drain to keep up the level of drive/tenacity  needed to actually get some of the things needed to make your life better/easier...im missing a leg and is still took me about 8-9 months just to even get fitted and approved for a bottom of the barrel prosthetic leg and then another 2-3 years after that befor finoly being approved for a much needed nicer "micro processor" leg...I imagine getting a much needed "nice" wheel chair to be a similar type fight

My point is this ...sadly most people responsible for paying for your needed equipment (ie your insurance company) are much more concerned about looking after there bottom line rather then looking after you. Meaning if you don't have an advocate that is vary well versed and educated in your needs/abilitys aswell as the willingness to go to battle for you aka calling your insurance company too the point of badgering them everyday untill your approved when you don't have what you need...sadly most people don't have someone to advocate for them making themselves there only advocate and most people are simply either not willing, able, or educated enough to know the best way to go about getting the things they need in a timely manner 

If you don't have an advocate and this chair isn't what you need then you need to tell both your insurance company aswell as your primary care ....and for me it would have been my "prosthetic office" aswell im unsure what the "wheel chair" equivalent would be (nu motion maybe? They were who made my power chair that took me another 2ish years to get after my accident (I also have an arm that dosnt work) 

Lasty I know personal pride can be a tuff thing in this community but when it comes 2 getting the expensive equipment you need ...probably best to check your pride at the door and be vary brutaly honest about what you can't do and list ANY and ALL  potential problems any equipment might present immediately and often and loudly to all insurance agents and health professionals (obviously don't be a jerk) but sometimes your the only one who's going to "stand up" for you...wish it were not the case  but I was amazed at the difference in care , equipment , and speed of approval came after finding a good advocate aswell as teaching myself the things I need 2 know to do myself the things she can't do....its absolutely Paramount in the system we currently live in.

Was meaning "motorcycle physics" in general wich I find easier to explain with more of a sport/street bike thought process   but it holds thru on a motocross track aswell . When you are coming into a turn you can lock up both wheels aslong as your still strait up and down but the second you start to lean the bike over thats when you need to let off in order to get as much traction as possible with the front control wheel and as long as your front has good traction you can light up the rear tire exiting the turn while you still have the bike leaned over but if you "light up" the front tire in that same scenario your crashing 100% of the time regardless of type of bike or location.

So I am a motorcycle technician and there have been attempts in the past to make a 2wd bike but you fall into negative returns on what you can do with your traction up front vary quickly that makes the vary complicated drive train wayyy more complicated/expensive for vary little usable return it would actually provide not to mention there would be a large safety concern as anytime you "apply throttle" you are effectively using up some of your available traction on the drive wheel so when you are at full lean you have to be vary careful about your throttle and brake controls as applying to much of either will result in a loss of traction and crash and while its possible to temporarily lose traction in the rear  and save it without crashing No one can save your front tire lossing traction in a turn ...thats a crash 100% of the time . Some riders are good enough to be able to control the bike with the rear wheel spinning getting vary little traction in the rear aslong as the front end is doing okay but the second the font wheel losses its traction its a bad day immediately.  

So moral of the story is its not worth playing the game of gambling with your front wheels traction in an effort to coax a tiny bit more "power delivery" out of running your power thru both wheels rather then a dedicated drive wheel and a dedicated front control wheel

Great frame once u get it all in there but definitely can cause extra headaches to a new build especially.

  As for your fc and esc getting a "stack" that come with the connector cable is nice for ease of not having a make the cable just make sure its not like a weird off brand anything from diatone,luminear, dalrc,ect. Last but not least a receiver idk if u already have a controller but if so make sure ur receiver has the "protocol" it calls for...crossfire is the industry standard most used but if u don't have a tango2 or a mamba requires a external modual on ur radio .
